descriptionMarkdown:
Damage Threshold: total all damage from one hit or effect after resistance, then compare it with DT. Below DT, the 
hull takes no damage. At least DT, apply the full total. DT is a threshold, not damage reduction. Do not combine 
separate attacks to overcome it.
Against a hull, Armour-Breaking also halves DT for that hit, rounded down. It does not reduce AC or bypass Full Cover. 
This extends the Chapter 7 property. Power Field and Monomolecular do not bypass DT unless explicitly stated. 
Personal weapons can harm hulls when they overcome DT.
Vehicles are objects. Hulls are immune to poison, disease, radiation, fear, Suppression and effects that target only 
creatures or minds. Psychic damage cannot harm a hull unless the power explicitly affects machinery or objects. 
Vehicles do not make death saves, recover through rests or benefit from creature-only healing. Drivers and exposed 
occupants suffer conditions normally; their personal resistances do not protect the hull.
Roll one breakdown when a critical hit damages the hull, or when it first reaches half maximum HP or less in an 
encounter. If it begins at half HP or less, roll on its first damaging hit instead. Maximum one breakdown roll per vehicle 
per round; simultaneous triggers give one roll. Critical hits otherwise double damage dice normally.
d6 Breakdown Effect
1 Running gear Speed is halved until repaired; minimum 5 ft unless already 0.
2 Steering Disadvantage on driving checks and vehicle Dexterity saves until repaired.
3 Weapon jam One random fitted mount cannot fire until Damage Control succeeds. With no mount, 
use result 2.
4 Hull breach Lose Sealed. One random enclosed occupant position provides only Heavy Cover until 
repaired.
5 Engine stall Speed becomes 0 and remaining movement is lost until Damage Control succeeds.
6 Vehicle fire At the end of the driver’s turn, hull takes 2d6 fire damage ignoring DT. If uncontrolled, 
use the former driver’s initiative. Damage Control extinguishes it.
Breakdowns do not stack with themselves. A repeated active result instead deals 2d6 hull damage ignoring DT; this 
cannot trigger another breakdown. Field or workshop repair clears running-gear, steering or hull-breach damage (21.8). 
Damage Control clears only jams, stalls and fires.
At 0 HP the vehicle is Wrecked: stop movement and disable its mounts. Each occupant makes a DC 13 Dexterity 
save, taking 2d6 bludgeoning on failure or half on success. Conscious occupants may immediately leave into an 
unoccupied space within 5 ft without an action. Anyone remaining must later leave normally or be rescued. Wrecks do 
not automatically explode. Fire or hazardous cargo may create a separately signalled danger.
Uncontrolled movement: when a vehicle would next move without a conscious driver, it coasts straight up to 30 ft, 
limited by the distance it moved last round, then stops. Resolve obstacles as collisions. A new driver at the controls 
before then can prevent the coast. Swapping drivers never grants a second movement allowance in the round.
